svg.title: Container vs Pod doodle infographic
svg.desc: Hand-drawn doodle style poster comparing a Container as a single delivery boy with a restaurant and food parcel, versus a Pod as a delivery partner surrounded by GPS, tracking, payment, and alerts inside a wobbly bubble.

g.style: font-family: 'Comic Sans MS', 'Marker Felt', 'Bradley Hand', cursive;fill:rgb(0, 0, 0);stroke:none;color:rgb(0, 0, 0);stroke-width:1px;stroke-linecap:butt;stroke-linejoin:miter;opacity:1;font-family:"Comic Sans MS", "Marker Felt", "Bradley Hand", cursive;font-size:16px;font-weight:400;text-anchor:start;dominant-baseline:auto
g.text: why kubernetes uses pods instead of managing containers directly
a container is like a delivery boy
a pod is a team of containers
container = one delivery boy doing one job alone
pod = delivery boy + GPS + tracking + payments as one team
most pods contain only one container
multiple containers only when they must work closely together
